gap: No result ChatGPT got states, from a named test, that the Shure MV7+ over XLR needed the gain knob at almost 80% on an SSL2+ interface to reach a decent level, and that this introduced distortion from the interface (The Podcast Host, Sarah Buchynski). That matters to a hybrid-mic buyer who plans to move to an interface later.
standout_why: I could not read either cited MusicRadar page (best-podcasting-microphones and best-usb-microphones). Both fetches returned only the page title, so I can't rule out that they mention gain. ProVideo Coalition reviewed the Q9U (2021) and the PodMic USB (2024) and gives no measured hum, noise, gain or latency figures. SoundGuys reviewed the MV7+ but shows Shure's frequency chart, not its own measurement. A search snippet from a different thepostflow.com page (the publisher of result #2) says qualitatively that the MV7+ 'still needs most of an interface's gain range' over XLR. So a rival likely covers part of this already, though not with a named interface and gain setting. None of the pages I checked has a lab-measured frequency response or self-noise figure for any of the candidates.
decides: This backs up ChatGPT's MV7+ pick for USB use: The Podcast Host found its auto gain landed at -24 LUFS with -4 dBFS true peak and no manual setup. It weakens the 'upgrade to an interface later' argument for the MV7+: on XLR it is gain-hungry, and a budget interface like the SSL2+ distorted at the gain it needed. A buyer who plans to go XLR-only should budget for a high-gain preamp or an inline booster. I found no comparable named measurement for the PodMic USB or Q9U, so this can't rank the three on XLR gain.

findings.label: Interface gain needed over XLR
findings.value: Gain knob at almost 80% on a Solid State Logic SSL2+ to set a decent signal level; the reviewer heard distortion from the interface at that gain
findings.note: Sarah Buchynski, page last updated 2024-05-07. A hands-on test, not a lab measurement. The knob position is not converted to dB and no distortion figure is given.

findings.label: Output level with Auto Level (auto gain) over USB
findings.note: Sarah Buchynski, updated 2024-05-07. The reviewer later boosted the noise-test clip to -16 LUFS. Podcast platforms usually normalise to about -14 to -18 LUFS, so auto gain leaves roughly 8 dB of headroom below a -16 LUFS target.

findings.label: Podcastage recording chain
findings.value: 24-bit / 48 kHz, gain -6 dB, boosted +8.5 dB in post
findings.note: Reviewer Bandrew Scott, page dated May 8 (no year shown). These are the reviewer's own settings, not a measured noise floor. The page does not say which output (USB or XLR) the settings belong to.

findings.label: Podcastage recording chain
findings.value: 24-bit / 48 kHz, computer level 51 dB, boosted +8 dB in post
findings.note: Reviewer Bandrew Scott, page dated Jul 25 (no year shown). The reviewer heard 'a little bit of grain on the top end (mainly in XLR mode)'. The page states the XLR port is inactive while the mic is connected over USB. No noise figure in the text.

findings.label: SoundGuys overall rating
findings.note: Dave Carr, published 2024-08-28, tested over 10 days with MOTIV Mix 1.1.2.916 beta. This is a scored rating, not a measurement. The frequency response chart on the page is Shure's, not SoundGuys'.

findings.label: Headphone output level in USB mode
findings.value: Loud enough at about 60% of the host device's volume with 32-ohm CB-1 headphones
findings.source_title: Review: Samson Q9U studio dynamic hybrid mic with A7WS windscreen (ProVideo Coalition)
findings.note: Allan Tépper, 2021-04-26. XLR was recorded through a RØDECaster Pro, USB on macOS Catalina at 48 kHz / 24-bit. The hum-sensitivity numbers on the page are Samson's specs, not the reviewer's measurements.

unsourced: Lab-measured frequency response or self-noise for the MV7+, PodMic USB, Q9U, Maono PD400X, PD200XS or Fifine AM8 from RTINGS, SoundGuys, Notebookcheck or a magazine lab. RTINGS does not test microphones. SoundGuys' MV7+ review uses Shure's chart, and I found no SoundGuys review of the PodMic USB or Q9U.

Interface gain the PodMic USB needs over XLR from a named test. AudioTechnology's review (audiotechnology.com/?p=76996, quoted in a snippet as 'Maxing the gain out at 63dB') returned HTTP 403. Rode PodMic USB equivalent noise (26 dBA XLR / 19 dBA USB per a search snippet). The Rode datasheet PDF would not parse, so the figure is not used.
